To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AOTM concept is a useful tool to describe the distribution of fresh fruits and vegetables in the state of Ohio, that value chain development is a promising approach for scaling-up distribution, that piggybacking is a useful strategy for scaling-up distribution and that the Ohio Food Policy Council can facilitate market development and support meaningful connections in the local food system.

the AOTM approach can be applied to distributors and retailers in a regional food system, that the concept of value-based spatially proximate relationships is important for regional food systems, and that a hybrid approach to food systems, such as pigging-back, may be a useful way to scale-up local food distribution.

(1) There is a need to develop and expand regional distribution of fresh produce in the state of Ohio, (2) There is a lack of information about the current distribution of fresh fruits and vegetables in Ohio, and (3) There is a desire among Ohio retailers for increased distribution of fresh fruits, vegetables and other local foods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for adaptive change within the food system.
the role that regional distribution plays in the development of local and regional food systems and how to improve and expand regional distribution of food in Ohio.
how we might scale-up regional food distribution systems and the role of the food system in facilitating such change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many ways to scale-up distribution and the Ohio Food Policy Council can play a role in facilitating these efforts.

there is great potential to scale-up distribution of locally grown fruits and vegetables in Ohio, and that the state can play an important role in facilitating this growth through policy and program support.

there is a clear opportunity in the Ohio food system to scale-up regional fruit and vegetables, and that the state of Ohio can facilitate this by providing targeted support to the AOTM firms that are interested in scaling-up and by providing support to the regional food system infrastructure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ohio Food Policy Council should support the development of a state-level distribution network that is designed to facilitate connections between producers, distributors and retail outlets, while providing support for the development of hybrid solutions to improve the flow of local food in the state.

we have demonstrated that the Ohio fresh fruit and vegetable distribution system can be improved and expanded to serve Ohioans, that the AOTM concept can be applied beyond the farm to include distributors and retailers and that hybrid solutions, such piggybacking, are viable and should be considered in scaling-up regional food systems.
there are opportunities to scale-up distribution of local food in Ohio, but that the state-level policy council needs to be more strategic about their efforts to support this.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a food policy council can be a key player in the food system by identifying and facilitating connections between food system actors and by providing a venue for the development and implementation of policy that can support these connections.
